# Intent - phase-m

Written 2026-10-30 by flint (draft for Rand's confirmation). One page at most. This is the "why" that frames every anchor beneath it; Jev questions are judged against anchors, not against this document, so keep it short and let the anchors carry the testable facts.

## What this plan is for

Rand's words (approved 2026-10-30): "atm-core should be able to delete its workarounds: when sc-lint is done, every item on its P1 list passes as the GitHub issue describes, with nothing hidden."

The P1 list is #786 and #720 (`PORT-010`), #198 (consumer setup hook and step runner) and #136 (manifest dependency ownership). On released sc-lint 0.8.2, atm-core keeps a lint exclusion, a local checker or Justfile glue for each. sc-lint remains a general-purpose tool: atm-core supplies the failing cases, and its repository-specific policy stays in consumer configuration.

## What success looks like

- On a release that includes Phase M, atm-core can remove its `PORT-010` exclusions for the #786 paths and the #720 same-name sibling shape in every scope, while real cross-platform parity gaps are still reported (ANC-014, ANC-018, ANC-020, ANC-021, GH-786.S3).
- atm-core can drop its local source-only ownership checker, because `global_dependency_ownership` offers an opt-in source-only scope, with all-files checking still the default (ANC-025, GH-136.src-only.2).
- Each of atm-core's three `[boundaries]` keys has a recorded coverage verdict, and every remaining gap has an issue (ANC-016, GH-136.audit-verify, GH-136.audit-gaps).
- Conditional on a new ADR approved by Rand that supersedes ADR-020 decisions 9 and 13 and REQ-CLI-021: atm-core can delete its `_py`, `sc_lint_clippy_prefix`, `_sc-lint-clippy` and `_sc-lint-py` Justfile glue for #198 (ANC-023, ANC-024, ANC-019, ANC-022, GH-198.*).
- Each sprint traces to its GitHub issue and carries a deterministic regression for the reported consumer failure.

## What is deliberately out of scope

- Suppressing findings by blanket exclusion, by disabling a rule, or by widening allowed roots for atm-core paths.
- #198 work (ANC-023, ANC-024, ANC-019, ANC-022, GH-198.*) before the superseding ADR is Accepted. Rand ruled (2026-10-30) that the #198 runner.export_env (PYO3_PYTHON) need is in scope (GH-198.export-env.3) and that pub POSIX-only helpers (S8) are exempt. His later rulings (2026-10-30) require an approved exception path for any knowing PORT-010 opt-out, so S8 is exempt through that path, not by blanket rule (ANC-018, ANC-021), and a consumer method to override behavior such as the sc_lint.* helper interpreter (ANC-019).
- Other atm-core gaps that are not on the P1 list (for example #783, #784, #195 and #385), the 0.8.3 release-platform work, and any new process or tooling changes.

## Anchors

Anchors for this plan live in `anchors.json` (record of truth) and are rendered to `anchors.md`. Requirements and ADRs that govern this plan are listed there too, under their own IDs. Per-item anchors quote Rand's approved sentences; GH-* records carry the GitHub issue acceptance text they cite. Rand locked the 18 active records on 2026-10-30: "we can lock the anchors, but if tuning requires updating them, they will need to be changed".

**Amend path for a locked anchor.** A change to a locked statement is a new version that needs Rand's approval. It invalidates every earlier gate and tuning run for that anchor, which must be re-run against the new version. A change to the quote (his words) is a new anchor that retires the old one (`retire --replaced-by`).

ANC-018, ANC-020 and ANC-021 are locked but pending definition: Rand has not yet defined the "approved exception path" they rest on. Their summaries say so.

records.check: A step-environment test shows a cargo clippy step receives PYO3_PYTHON set to the runner.python interpreter when configured.
records.context: Issue acceptance text: https://github.com/randlee/sc-lint/issues/198#issuecomment-6513016954 C + mismatch paragraph; in scope per Rand 2026-10-30 (re-registered from GH-198.export-env.3, ID-only change)
records.deterministic_check: A step-environment test shows a cargo clippy step receives PYO3_PYTHON set to the runner.python interpreter when configured.

fail: Leaves PYO3_PYTHON unset for clippy, so atm-core keeps sc_lint_clippy_prefix.
pass: sc-lint can export the runner.python interpreter as PYO3_PYTHON to native steps such as cargo clippy. Evidence: test runner_export_env_pyo3 passes, showing the clippy step's env has PYO3_PYTHON set to the venv interpreter.

records.quote:
`runner.python` only rewrites step argv; cargo clippy needs the venv interpreter exported as `PYO3_PYTHON` and the venv dir on PATH for native (non-python) steps.
[…]
We need one more knob, e.g. `runner.export_env = ["PYO3_PYTHON"]` (plus the PATH prepend in (2) applied to every step), or a per-step `env`.
records.scope: The item changes step environment, runner config, or clippy steps in crates/sc-lint.
records.statement: sc-lint must be able to export the [tool.sc-lint].runner.python venv interpreter as PYO3_PYTHON to native (non-python) steps such as cargo clippy.

criteria.no: The compliance claim is asserted without anything checkable, or no compliance claim is made.
criteria.unclear: Something that might be evidence is mentioned, but it is not clear that it supports the compliance claim.
criteria.yes: The description points to at least one checkable artifact (path, diff, command, test, comparison) that supports the compliance claim.

evidenced.instructions: Where `item.text` claims the directive in `anchor.statement` was followed, does it cite concrete, checkable evidence for that claim: file paths, commit or diff references, commands that were run, test names or output, or a comparison against the required source? A bare assertion such as 'we followed the anchor' or 'based on X' with nothing checkable does not count. If the description does not claim the directive was followed at all, answer no.

criteria.no: The description is silent about the directive, or says it was deferred, skipped, or left for later.
criteria.unclear: The description mentions the directive's topic but it is not possible to tell whether the directive was followed.
criteria.yes: The description states that the work did what the directive requires, with the directive's specific content present.

implemented.instructions: According to `item.text`, was the directive in `anchor.statement` followed in what was actually built? Look for the directive's specific content in the account of the work: the required starting point was used, the required method was applied, the constraint was kept. A statement of intent or a plan to do it later does not count as followed. Judge whether the account says the directive was followed, not whether the account proves it.

criteria.no: The work is in a different part of the system or a different activity, and it could neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The description is too vague to tell what the work touched.
criteria.yes: The work changed, created, removed, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about.

relevant.instructions: The state holds a description of delivered work (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the delivered work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge compliance.

criteria.no: Nothing in the description conflicts with the directive, whether or not the directive is mentioned.
criteria.unclear: The description is ambiguous enough that the work might or might not conflict with the directive.
criteria.yes: The description states an action, approach, or decision in the delivered work that cannot be reconciled with the directive.

violated.instructions: Does `item.text` show that the work did something `anchor.statement` rules out, or used a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the work was written from scratch; the anchor forbids a dependency and the work added it; the anchor fixes a boundary and the work crossed it. Silence about the directive is not a violation. Judge conflict only.
